2_correctness.model_free_lemma: Correct, and checked against the definitions (Inextensible.lean:163-186). Inextensible := CausalCurveIn ∧ ¬ Extensible. Take a strict extension (I', c'). c' is a C-causal curve of the same W over I', so it is constant on I' (CausalCurveIn.eq_of_causalCurveOn_eq, which goes from segments to I' through `curve`). With t ∈ I (I non-empty, from CausalCurveIn.nonempty), c' t' = c' (φ t) = c t, which contradicts `grows`. The hypothesis is non-vacuous: the rational line meets it (rationalLine_causalCurveOn_eq, library) and so does the spacelike line (spacelikeLine_causalCurveOn_eq, new, from spacelikeLine_le). It is also a real restriction: the timelike line does not meet it. Over a reversed segment (a > b), Icc a b = ∅ and the hypothesis puts no condition there, which is right. The two-causality form and the stronger CurveNestedOn form are correct compositions of the library's causalCurveOn_of_forall_eq and CurveNestedOn.causalCurveIn.
2_correctness.converse: InextensibleNestedOn.leNested_of_causallyArcConnected takes [T1Space M] [SecondCountableTopology M], C.InextensibleNestedOn C' ⊤ and C.CausallyArcConnected, and concludes C.LeNested C'. It is the composition of the library's InextensibleNestedOn.curveNestedOn_of_t1_secondCountable (SubArc.lean:484, the ladder's [[implies]] inextensible_nested ⇒ curve_nested with standing T1, second_countable) and CurveNestedOn.leNested_of_causallyArcConnected (NestedConverse.lean:141). The open form composes the same lemma with CurveNestedOn.le_of_causallyArcConnectedOn. The claim is strong in appearance only: it is the ladder's existing edge followed by the existing consequence at curve_nested. Its standing is exactly the first lemma's instance binders, and nothing is asked of C'. Its contrapositive, that a counterexample on such a space has a narrower causality that is not causally arc-connected, is correct, and the rational line is such a causality (rationalLine_not_causallyArcConnected, NestedConverse.lean:353).

findings.what: The REPORT says 'over I = ∅ every curve is vacuously extensible'. That holds only when W is non-empty. Over I = ∅, Extensible W ∅ c holds iff W has a point, since a constant curve over {0} strictly extends it. For W = ⊥ there is no causal curve at all, so nothing is extensible. I checked both cases in a probe under the campaign directory, since deleted. The Lean statements and docstrings are not affected, and the hypothesis I.Nonempty of not_extensible_of_causalCurveOn_eq is still needed. The imprecision is in REPORT prose only, and it appears in neither the keeper's comment_proposal nor the kb_proposal.
findings.fix: If the remark is carried into the journal or a kb entry, write 'over I = ∅ every curve is vacuously extensible when W is non-empty'.
